decisions.decision: Scope this engagement to the Community Care Fund rebuild only; the separate 45-finding Org Health Assessment is current-state context for design, not in-scope remediation work.
decisions.rationale: Client confirmed; the two documents are distinct workstreams from different dates with no cross-reference in the interview.

sessions.summary: Full strategy run -- strategic context, approved vision statement, and business case for the CCF rebuild. Skipped research (Discovery Brief already carried sufficient client-specific detail).

decisions.decision: Approved vision: 'By the time the Community Care Fund reaches 1,000 applications a year, every eligibility decision, panel score, and audit follow-up is defensible on demand -- and a recipient gets paid without the SAP paperwork round-trip that costs weeks today.'
decisions.rationale: Approved as drafted, no wordsmithing requested.

decisions.decision: Revised the initial 4th strategic priority (platform scale-readiness) out of the ranked list and replaced it with 'give external panellists a proper review workspace' -- scale-readiness was an outcome-level framing already captured in the vision and current-state challenges, not a peer-level fix.
decisions.rationale: User asked to focus on strategic priorities before approving; caught a mixed-abstraction-level list on self-review (MECE constraint) and fixed it before presenting.
rejected: Keeping platform scale-readiness as a 4th ranked priority alongside the three specific gap-closures

open_threads: Noticed an unexplained stray line ('/notes: some grounding issue on this') under Users and Roles in outputs/00-discovery-brief.md that wasn't authored by this session -- flagged to the user, left untouched pending their direction.
next_steps: Run requirements to define epics grounded in this strategy.

sessions.summary: Defined 6 epics (E01 Intake & Case Creation, E02 Eligibility Screening, E03 Full Application Capture, E04 Review & Panel Decisioning, E05 Grant Disbursement, E06 Post-Funding Audit Tracking) and ran gap analysis via 6 parallel epic-analyst agents. Saved epics.json (6 epics) + gaps.json (79 gaps: 8 Source Conflict, 30 Missing Requirement, 10 Logical Gap, 9 Ambiguity, 7 Capability Gap, 10 Potential Risk, 5 Assumption).

decisions.decision: Approved the 6-epic skeleton as drafted, after confirming E02's eligibility-rule wording stays neutral pending client confirmation rather than silently picking 'funded' or 'submitted'.
decisions.rationale: User specifically asked to review E02 in full before approving and confirmed the HLR's funded-vs-submitted conflict should be flagged as an open question, not resolved by Scopezilla.

decisions.decision: Demoted HLR Capabilities 6-8 (REQ-35 through REQ-45 -- generic governance/compliance/data-quality/usability boilerplate) to gaps rather than epic-izing them.
decisions.rationale: No concrete process, owner, or metric behind any of these requirements -- a stub per the persona's 'a stub is a gap, not scope' rule.
rejected: Creating a 7th epic for platform governance/compliance boilerplate

decisions.decision: Recommended a Phase 0 to the client given 79 gaps and 8 source conflicts, both clearing the stated thresholds.
decisions.rationale: User chose this over proceeding straight to design; several gaps (2-year rule wording, panel cadence, SAP integration topology, payment gateway identity, scoring editability) are load-bearing to sizing and shouldn't be guessed at in design.
rejected: Proceeding straight to design with all gaps carried as disclosed assumptions

open_threads: 8 Source Conflicts need direct client resolution before design: G0101/G0104 (E01 email-intake behavior, EOI attachment wording), G0201 (E02 funded-vs-submitted 2-year rule), G0302 (E03 no-partial-save vs. standard save-for-later), G0401 (E04 panel cadence, same conflict as the Discovery Brief), G0406 (E04 score editability vs. panel-scoring-integrity priority), G0501 (E05 integration topology -- Salesforce-to-gateway vs. Salesforce-to-SAP-only), G0601 (E06 single-tier vs. three-tier escalation).

3 architecture forks stayed ungrounded (no KB atom found): G0312 (two-party e-signature for the Full Application, Public Sector/Grantmaking-scoped), G0502/G0503 (SAP vendor-identity validation mechanism and master-record ownership) -- recommend targeted KB/architecture queries at design time.
6 discipline-gap questions raised for a deliberate client conversation (not auto-scoped): experience design (G0111, G0210, G0314, G0415) and governance (G0112, G0209, G0315, G0414, G0514, G0605).
next_steps: Recommend Phase 0 to the client to close the highest-priority source conflicts and the two ungrounded architecture forks before sizing.
Run design to produce the architecture and T-shirt estimates for these epics once Phase 0 (or client confirmation on the key conflicts) lands.
Say 'generate clarification questions' to turn gaps.json into a client-facing question list for the Discovery Brief's Open Questions section.

sessions.summary: Turned all 79 gaps.json entries into client-facing questions, written into outputs/00-discovery-brief.md's Open Questions section (grouped: 8 source conflicts first, then missing requirements, ambiguities, risks, capability questions, assumptions, plus the 3 pre-existing non-requirements open items). Also stripped internal [KA-XXXX] provenance tags found in the brief's Research Findings section (pre-existing, from an earlier session) per the no-internal-provenance rule.
friction: validate-data.py flagged 13 pricing-leak false positives in the brief -- all are client business dollar figures (grant amounts, $50K/$100K review thresholds) from discovery, not invented Salesforce engagement pricing. Judged non-blocking and proceeded; noted for awareness.
next_steps: Send the Open Questions section to Rachel Doyle for the 8 source conflicts especially -- these are load-bearing to sizing.
Run design once the client has resolved or consciously deferred the key conflicts.

sessions.summary: Produced the architecture skeleton and T-shirt estimates for all 6 epics, saved to outputs/01-solution.md and data/estimates.json. Base pattern: Public Sector Grantmaking module (Platform + Experience Cloud). Ran targeted central-KB searches for the two gaps the earlier requirements pass left ungrounded (ABN/registry validation, 2km polygon boundary pattern) -- both confirmed genuinely ungrounded (no on-point atom on an in-scope cloud) rather than assumed covered.
friction: validate-data.py again flagged a pricing-leak false positive in 01-solution.md (the client's own $50K panel-routing threshold) -- same judgment as the prior session, non-blocking.

decisions.decision: Adopted Public Sector Grantmaking (Platform + Experience Cloud) as the base architecture pattern, flagged as a licensing decision the client needs to confirm since the org doesn't have this module provisioned today.
decisions.rationale: Standard Salesforce fit for the full grant lifecycle (intake, review, award, disbursement, progress reporting), grounded via KA-9728.

decisions.decision: Recommended a validation-rule/Flow lock on panel scores that resolves the editability source conflict (G0406) regardless of which reading the client confirms -- both readings agree a score shouldn't change after the decision point, they only disagree on when that point is.
decisions.rationale: Lets the architecture proceed without waiting on G0406's resolution, since the mechanism is correct either way; only the exact trigger point still needs confirming.
rejected: Waiting on G0406 resolution before designing any score-integrity mechanism

open_threads: E05 (Grant Disbursement) sized XL with Unknown confidence -- the integration topology (Salesforce-to-gateway vs. Salesforce-to-SAP-only) and payment gateway identity are both unresolved and this is the single largest open risk in the engagement.
3 new load-bearing assumptions persisted to gaps.json (G0114, G0115, G0417): Public Sector Grantmaking licensing, Experience Cloud guest-user baseline, and the panel-score lock trigger point.
T-shirt distribution: 1 XL (E05), 1 L (E04), 4 M (E01, E02, E03, E06).
next_steps: Run roadmap to phase the epics and derive a top-down duration range.
Resolve E05's integration topology and gateway identity before this size can be finalized with confidence.

terminology.CCF: Community Care Fund — the grant program being rebuilt
terminology.CML: Community Marketing Lead — the 4 regional staff who triage eligibility and chase applications
terminology.EOI: Expression of Interest — Stage 1 of the two-stage CCF application process
terminology.two-kilometre rule: Eligibility criterion requiring a project be within 2km of a Northwind Grid asset (substation, transmission corridor)
terminology.special project: An undocumented, Head-of-Communications-discretion exception allowing re-application within 2 years of prior funding
terminology.panel: The 11-person approval body (6 internal, 5 external) that reviews grants over $50K
terminology.DigiTech: Northwind Grid's existing Salesforce implementation partner
